analyst_view.overall: Early view: Le Havre are bottom with 2 points and five straight defeats, and Didier Digard was removed at the end of October with academy director Jair Karam in interim charge. The club says a new coach should be in place from late November (one report names Valerien Ismael), so this could be one of his first home games. Le Mans, promoted and 15th, have drawn five of ten, including 1-1 with Monaco last time.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. These are two of the weaker attacks in the league (9 and 12 goals), Le Mans have been drawing games, and a new Le Havre coach is likely to start by tightening the defence. I lean slightly lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners. Le Havre should push at home, but nothing in the news points away from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. A December game between the bottom side and a promoted team fighting to stay up should be tense and stop-start, so I lean higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots, most of them from Le Havre. A home side desperate for a first win should shoot plenty, but Le Mans are compact; I keep the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. Neither side finishes well, but the home side should get enough efforts on goal to land near the number.
